title: Eggs Benedict
summary: Toasted English muffins layered with ham, poached eggs and buttery lemon hollandaise.
method: Melt the butter and let it cool slightly. Whisk the egg yolks with the lemon juice over low heat for a few minutes.
Slowly whisk in the warm butter until thick and silky, keeping it below a simmer.
Split the English muffins and toast until golden at the edges.
Warm the ham in a dry skillet over medium heat until heated through, then arrange on the muffin halves.
Bring a wide pan of water to a bare simmer over medium heat and add the vinegar. Slide in the eggs from small cups and cook until the whites set and the yolks stay soft.
Lift the eggs out, blot off excess water and place on the ham. Spoon over the hollandaise and finish with the cayenne.

stages.title: Prepare hollandaise
steps: Melt butter and let it cool slightly while whisking egg yolks with lemon over gentle heat.
Slowly whisk in warm butter until thick and silky, keeping the mixture below a simmer.

stages.title: Toast and warm ham
steps: Split and toast muffins until golden at the edges.
Warm ham in a dry skillet and arrange on muffin halves.

stages.title: Poach the eggs
steps: Bring a wide pan of water to a bare simmer and add vinegar.
Crack eggs into small cups and slide into water, cooking until whites set and yolks remain soft.

stages.title: Assemble immediately
steps: Lift eggs out with a slotted spoon and blot excess water.
Place on ham, spoon over hollandaise and finish with cayenne.

tips: Keep hollandaise warm, not hot, to avoid splitting.
variations: Use smoked salmon instead of ham.
storage: Best eaten immediately; do not store assembled eggs Benedict.

title: Cacio e pepe
summary: Silky spaghetti coated in Pecorino Romano, freshly cracked black pepper and starchy pasta water.
method: Crush the peppercorns and toast in a wide dry pan over medium heat for about 1 minute, until fragrant. Add a ladle of hot pasta water.
Boil the spaghetti in lightly salted water until just shy of al dente, about 8 to 10 minutes. Reserve 2 cups of the cooking water, then drain.
Mix the Pecorino with a little warm (not boiling) pasta water into a thick, smooth paste.
Off the heat, toss the pasta in the pepper water, then stir in the cheese paste gradually.
Add small splashes of pasta water until glossy and creamy. Serve immediately.

stages.title: Toast the pepper
steps: Crush peppercorns coarsely and toast in a wide dry pan over medium heat for about 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add a ladle of hot pasta water to release their aroma.

stages.title: Cook pasta
steps: Boil spaghetti in lightly salted water until just shy of al dente.
Reserve at least two cups of starchy cooking water before draining.

stages.title: Make cheese paste
steps: Mix finely grated Pecorino with a little warm, not boiling, pasta water.
Stir until a thick smooth paste forms without clumping.

stages.title: Emulsify and serve
steps: Toss pasta in pepper water off the heat, then stir in cheese paste gradually.
Add small splashes of pasta water until glossy and creamy; serve immediately.

tips: Keep cheese away from direct heat to prevent clumps.
storage: Best eaten fresh; leftovers can become grainy.

title: Dan dan noodles
summary: Wheat noodles tossed in chilli oil, sesame paste and savoury pork with Sichuan pepper.
method: Whisk the sesame paste, soy sauce, vinegar and chilli oil with a little warm water until smooth and pourable. Divide between four bowls.
Fry the pork mince in a pan over high heat for 5 minutes, breaking it into crumbles, until browned.
Add the garlic and Sichuan pepper and cook for 1 minute until fragrant and the pork is cooked through.
Boil the noodles until springy and tender. Reserve a little noodle water, then drain.
Add the noodles to the sauce bowls and top with the hot pork. Toss, loosening with noodle water, and finish with the spring onions.

stages.title: Mix the sauce
steps: Whisk sesame paste, soy sauce, vinegar and chilli oil with warm water.
Adjust until smooth and pourable, then divide between bowls.

stages.title: Brown the pork
steps: Fry pork mince in a hot pan over high heat for 5 minutes, breaking it into small crumbles, until browned.
Add garlic and Sichuan pepper and cook until fragrant and pork is fully cooked.

stages.title: Cook noodles
steps: Boil noodles according to their packet until springy and tender.
Reserve a little noodle water and drain well.

stages.title: Toss and serve
steps: Add noodles to sauce bowls and spoon over hot pork.
Toss thoroughly, loosening with noodle water and topping with spring onions.

tips: Use Chinese sesame paste for a robust toasted flavour.
variations: Swap pork for finely chopped mushrooms.
storage: Refrigerate pork topping up to 3 days; cook noodles fresh.

title: Chicken biryani
summary: Fragrant basmati rice layered with spiced chicken, caramelised onions, saffron and fresh mint.
method: Marinate the chicken in the yoghurt, ginger-garlic paste, biryani masala and turmeric for at least 30 minutes in the fridge.
Soak the rice briefly, then boil in salted water until about 70% cooked. Drain while the grains are still firm.
Fry the sliced onions on medium-high heat until deeply golden. Cook the marinated chicken until nearly cooked through.
Layer the chicken, rice, onions, mint and saffron steeped in the milk in a heavy pot.
Cover tightly and cook on very low heat until the chicken is cooked through and the rice is tender.
Rest covered for 10 minutes, then fluff gently.

stages.title: Marinate chicken
steps: Mix chicken with yoghurt, ginger-garlic paste, biryani masala and turmeric.
Refrigerate for at least thirty minutes while preparing rice and onions.

stages.title: Parboil rice
steps: Rinse and soak basmati rice briefly, then boil in salted water until about seventy percent cooked.
Drain promptly so grains remain firm enough to finish steaming.

stages.title: Layer the biryani
steps: Fry sliced onions on medium-high heat until deeply golden and cook marinated chicken until nearly cooked through.
Layer chicken, rice, onions, mint and saffron-infused milk in a heavy pot.

stages.title: Steam and rest
steps: Cover tightly and cook on very low heat until chicken is cooked through and rice tender.
Rest covered ten minutes, then fluff gently without crushing the grains.

tips: Keep rice slightly undercooked before layering.
variations: Add boiled eggs and toasted cashews.
storage: Refrigerate promptly up to 2 days; reheat thoroughly.

title: Baba ganoush
summary: Smoky roasted aubergine blended with tahini, lemon and garlic for a silky dip.
method: Prick the aubergines and roast at 220°C for about 35 minutes, until the skins collapse and the flesh is very soft. For extra smokiness, char the skins over a gas flame first.
Cool the aubergines, scoop out the flesh and drain briefly in a sieve.
Mash the flesh with the tahini, lemon juice, grated garlic and cumin until creamy but still slightly textured.
Season with salt, adding more lemon if needed, then drizzle with olive oil and scatter over the parsley.
Serve with warm flatbread, if using.

stages.title: Char the aubergines
steps: Prick aubergines and roast at 220°C until skins collapse and flesh is very soft.
For a smokier flavour, char the skins over a gas flame first, turning until blackened all over.

stages.title: Drain the flesh
steps: Cool until manageable, then scoop out the soft flesh.
Drain in a sieve briefly to remove excess liquid and bitterness.

stages.title: Mix the dip
steps: Mash aubergine with tahini, lemon juice, grated garlic and cumin.
Stir until creamy but still slightly textured.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Taste for salt and lemon and drizzle with olive oil.
Scatter parsley on top and serve with warm flatbread.

tips: Drain roasted aubergine to avoid a watery dip.
variations: Add a spoon of yoghurt for extra creaminess.
storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days in an airtight container.

title: Coconut rice
summary: Fluffy jasmine rice gently cooked in coconut milk with a delicate sweetness and pandan aroma.
method: Rinse the jasmine rice until the water runs mostly clear, then drain well.
Combine the coconut milk, water, sugar and salt in a heavy saucepan, adding the pandan leaf if using.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Add the rice, cover tightly and cook on very low heat for about 15 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Don't lift the lid.
Remove from the heat and rest covered for 10 minutes, then discard the pandan and fluff with a fork.

stages.title: Rinse the rice
steps: Rinse jasmine rice gently until the water runs mostly clear.
Drain well so the liquid ratio stays accurate.

stages.title: Combine liquids
steps: Stir coconut milk, water, sugar and salt in a heavy saucepan.
Add pandan leaf if using and bring just to a gentle simmer over medium heat.

stages.title: Steam the rice
steps: Add rice, cover tightly and reduce heat to very low.
Cook without lifting the lid until liquid is absorbed and rice tender.

stages.title: Rest and fluff
steps: Remove from heat and leave covered for ten minutes.
Discard pandan and fluff gently with a fork before serving.

tips: Use full-fat coconut milk for richer flavour.
variations: Add lime zest for a fresh note.
storage: Refrigerate promptly up to 2 days; reheat thoroughly.

title: Chicken yakitori
summary: Chargrilled chicken skewers brushed with a glossy soy, mirin and sake glaze.
method: Simmer the soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar over medium heat for about 10 minutes, until slightly syrupy. Set some aside clean for serving.
Cut the chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces and the spring onions into short lengths. Thread them alternately onto soaked bamboo skewers.
Grill over medium-high heat for 10 to 12 minutes, turning regularly, until golden and cooked through with no pink inside.
Brush with the glaze in the final few minutes until shiny, without burning.
Rest briefly, then brush with the reserved clean glaze and serve.

stages.title: Prepare the glaze
steps: Simmer soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar until slightly syrupy.
Set aside some clean sauce for serving and use the rest for basting.

stages.title: Thread the skewers
steps: Cut chicken into even bite-sized pieces and spring onions into short lengths.
Thread alternating pieces onto soaked bamboo skewers.

stages.title: Grill the chicken
steps: Grill over medium-high heat for 10 to 12 minutes, turning regularly so all sides cook evenly until golden and cooked through.
Brush with glaze during the final minutes to build a shiny coating without burning.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Check chicken is fully cooked through before removing from heat.
Rest briefly and brush with reserved clean glaze.

tips: Glaze near the end to prevent sugar scorching.
storage: Refrigerate cooked skewers up to 3 days; reheat thoroughly.

title: Lebanese chicken shawarma bowls
summary: Spiced grilled chicken over rice with cucumber, tomato, pickles and garlicky yoghurt sauce.
method: Mix the chicken with half the yoghurt, garlic, lemon, cumin, paprika and cinnamon. Refrigerate for 20 minutes while you prep the rest.
Rinse the rice and cook over low heat, covered, until fluffy, about 12 minutes.
Dice the cucumber and tomatoes and season lightly with lemon.
Cook the chicken in a hot skillet or grill pan over high heat until charred in places and cooked through, about 15 minutes. Rest for 5 minutes, then slice across the grain.
Mix the remaining yoghurt with garlic and lemon for a sauce. Serve the chicken over rice with the salad and drizzle with sauce.

stages.title: Marinate chicken
steps: Mix chicken with half the yoghurt, garlic, lemon, cumin, paprika and cinnamon.
Rest refrigerated while rice and vegetables are prepared.

stages.title: Cook rice and salad
steps: Rinse basmati rice and cook, covered, over low heat until fluffy.
Dice cucumber and tomatoes and season lightly with lemon.

stages.title: Grill chicken
steps: Cook chicken in a hot skillet or grill pan until charred in places and fully cooked through.
Rest five minutes before slicing across the grain.

stages.title: Assemble bowls
steps: Mix remaining yoghurt with garlic and lemon for a quick sauce.
Serve chicken over rice with salad and drizzle with sauce.

tips: Chicken thighs stay juicy under high heat.
storage: Refrigerate cooked chicken and rice separately up to 3 days; reheat thoroughly.

title: Gnocchi with brown butter and sage
summary: Pillowy potato gnocchi tossed in nutty browned butter with crisp sage leaves and Parmesan.
ingredients: 1 tbsp salt, for the cooking water
method: Grate the parmesan, zest the lemon and cut it into wedges. Dry the sage leaves and cut the butter into pieces.
Bring 3 litres of water to the boil over high heat and add the salt.
Melt the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat until foaming. Cook the sage for 1–2 minutes, until crisp and the butter is nutty and golden brown. Lift the sage out onto paper towel.
Cook the gnocchi in the boiling water for 2–3 minutes, until they float. Scoop out 100 ml of cooking water, then lift the gnocchi out.
Return the pan to medium heat and toss the gnocchi with the reserved water for 1–2 minutes, until lightly golden and glossy.
Off the heat, stir through the zest, half the parmesan and pepper. Serve topped with the sage, remaining parmesan and lemon wedges.

stages.title: Prepare the ingredients
steps: Finely grate the parmesan into a bowl.
Zest the lemon with a fine grater, then cut the lemon into wedges for serving.
Pick the 16 sage leaves and pat them dry with paper towel so they crisp rather than spit.
Cut the butter into 4 or 5 pieces so it melts evenly.

stages.title: Brown the butter and crisp the sage
steps: Bring 3 litres water to the boil in a large pot over high heat and stir in the salt.
Melt the butter in a large frying pan over medium heat, swirling occasionally, until it foams.
Add the sage leaves and cook for 1–2 minutes, until the leaves are crisp and the butter smells nutty and turns golden brown.
Remove the pan from the heat and lift the sage out onto paper towel, leaving the butter in the pan.

stages.title: Cook the gnocchi
steps: Add the gnocchi to the boiling water and cook for 2–3 minutes, until they float to the surface.
Scoop out 100 ml of the cooking water, then lift the gnocchi out with a slotted spoon.

stages.title: Toss and serve
steps: Return the pan of brown butter to medium heat and add the gnocchi with the reserved cooking water.
Toss gently for 1–2 minutes, until the gnocchi are lightly golden and coated in a glossy sauce.
Take the pan off the heat and stir through the lemon zest, half the parmesan and a good grind of black pepper.
Divide among 4 bowls, scatter over the crisp sage and the remaining parmesan, and serve with the lemon wedges.

tips: Pat the sage dry before frying, as water makes the butter spit and the leaves go limp instead of crisp.
Watch the butter closely once it foams. It goes from golden to burnt in under a minute, so pull the pan off the heat as soon as it smells nutty.
The starchy cooking water helps the butter and gnocchi come together into a smooth, glossy sauce rather than a greasy one.
Lifting the gnocchi out with a slotted spoon avoids draining the pot and keeps them from sticking together.
variations: Add 100 g toasted walnuts, roughly chopped, for crunch and a nutty flavour.
Stir through 2 handfuls of baby spinach with the gnocchi and cook for 1 minute until wilted.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat in a frying pan over medium heat with a splash of water for 3–4 minutes until piping hot. The sage will soften.
